messages.content:
Risk: Confidential data in prompt
Description: Confidential information might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.
Concern: If not properly developed to secure confidential data, the model might reveal confidential information or IP in the generated output. Additionally, end users' confidential information might be unintentionally collected and stored.
Policy: Clinical Staff Credentials & Institutional Data

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#CWE-213: Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies — The product's intended functionality exposes information to certain actors in accordance with the developer's security policy, but this information is regarded as sensitive according to the intended security policies of other stakeholders such as the product's administrator, users, or others whose information is being processed. [found by 4/9 queries]
  Siblings: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor, Device Unlock Credential Sharing, Exposure of Sensitive System Information Due to Uncleared Debug Information
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS — Adversaries may exfiltrate private information via [AI Model Inference API Access](/techniques/AML.T0040).
AI Models have been shown leak private information about their training data (e.g.  [Infer Training Data Membership](/techniques/AML.T0024.000), [Invert AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.001)).
The model itself may also be extracted ([Extract AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.002)) for the purposes of [AI Intellectual Property Theft](/techniques/AML.T0048.004).

Exfiltration of information relating to private training data raises privacy concerns.
Private training data may include personally identifiable information, or other protected data. [found by 3/9 queries]
  Siblings: LLM Response Rendering - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS, LLM Data Leakage - ATLAS
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/SEC/Funds/CollectiveInvestmentVehicles/RiskLevel: risk level — None [found by 3/9 queries]
  Siblings: moneyness, market level classifier, occurrence kind
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0057: LLM Data Leakage - ATLAS — Adversaries may craft prompts that induce the LLM to leak sensitive information.
This can include private user data or proprietary information.
The leaked information may come from proprietary training data, data sources the LLM is connected to, or information from other users of the LLM. [found by 2/9 queries]
  Siblings: LLM Response Rendering - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024.001: Invert AI Model - ATLAS — AI models' training data could be reconstructed by exploiting the confidence scores that are available via an inference API.
By querying the inference API strategically, adversaries can back out potentially private information embedded within the training data.
This could lead to privacy violations if the attacker can reconstruct the data of sensitive features used in the algorithm. [found by 2/9 queries]
  Siblings: Extract AI Model - ATLAS, Infer Training Data Membership - ATLAS

axes.rationale: This class directly addresses the risk of sensitive information being leaked by the LLM, focusing on how adversaries craft prompts to induce this leakage. The 'agent' role highlights the adversarial actor involved.

This class describes how private information embedded in the training data can be reconstructed through strategic querying of the inference API. The 'object' role represents the sensitive information itself that is being targeted.
